race_context: Northwestern School Corporation is a Howard County district northwest of Kokomo covering Clay, Ervin and Howard Townships {sboe_plan}{wiki_nwsc}. It runs Northwestern Elementary, Howard Elementary, Northwestern Middle School and Northwestern High School {wiki_nwsc}. GreatSchools lists 1,847 students in grades PK-12 (year not stated) {greatschools_nwsc}. Wikipedia lists Kristen Bilkey as superintendent, and The Kokomo Lantern identified her as superintendent in 2022 {wiki_nwsc}{lantern_2022}; this guide could not open the district website to confirm who leads the district in 2026. This is not Shelby County's Northwestern Consolidated School Corporation.

The board has five members serving four-year terms: one resident each of Clay, Ervin and Howard Townships and two at-large members. Under a plan the board adopted in May 2022 and the State Board of Education reviewed in June 2022, all five are elected by voters across the whole district {sboe_plan}. The township seats were filled in November 2024: Daniel J Armstrong (Clay), Jonathan C Eller (Ervin) and Jonathan T Underwood (Howard) {enr_2024}{kt_2025_new}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: both at-large seats. The Howard County election office lists the race as 'Northwestern School Corporation, At Large (2 seats)', so voters choose two, not one as shown on the state list {howard_2026}{in_list}. The seats are held by Kenneth E Ortman and Ted D Merrell, who won them in November 2022 with 1,873 and 1,661 votes, ahead of incumbent Jenny L Kelly (1,063) and Elke R Fahrmann (503) {enr_2022}{kt_2022_results}. Both incumbents are running again, and they are the only two candidates, so the race is uncontested in effect {howard_2026}{in_list}.

Party labels: Merrell filed as a Republican; Ortman checked the box choosing not to disclose any party affiliation and is listed by the state as Nonpartisan {merrell_petition}{ortman_petition}{in_list}.

Facilities: in September 2022 The Kokomo Lantern reported a $51 million facilities project to upgrade every building in the district; Bilkey called the work 'necessities that improve the overall campus, security, and the student experience' {lantern_2022}. The rest of that article is behind a paywall.
Budget: this guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Northwestern, and no operating or safety referendum.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or campaign website for either candidate.

Was elected in November 2022 as a newcomer, receiving the most votes (28%) in a four-person race for two at-large seats {kt_2022_results}{enr_2022}.
